key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Third District
key_cases.holding: Dismissal of a private dependency petition filed two days before the youth turned eighteen was affirmed because the record supported the finding that he had not been abandoned, abused or neglected by his mother.
key_cases.relevance: Where the statutory grounds are not proved, the correct outcome is dismissal rather than adjudication.
key_cases.quote: we agree that S.A.R.D. failed to establish that he is a dependent child under Chapter 39, Florida Statutes (2015)

key_cases.case_name: R.F. v. Florida Department of Children & Families
key_cases.holding: Proof that a parent sexually abused one child does not by itself establish that a sibling is dependent; the court must examine all the circumstances to decide whether the parent poses a substantial risk of imminent abuse or neglect to the other child.
key_cases.relevance: Where the circumstances do not show substantial risk to the sibling, the petition as to that child must fail.
key_cases.quote: While the commission of such an act may be highly relevant, it is not automatically dispositive of the issue of dependency.
